assessments.reasoning: The dated W3C launch paragraph calls the Core Specification an official standard and introduces WebAssembly as a language, described there as low-level. The exact Core Recommendation separately calls WebAssembly a programming language with text and binary forms.

challenge.method: Compare the exact announcement paragraph with the Recommendation’s dated header, status wording, publication history and the distinct JavaScript and Web API publications. Challenge a platform-only, runtime-only or testing-script identity reading.

The body preserves older Proposed Recommendation wording alongside its actual Recommendation endorsement. APIs and scripting remain separate scopes. Active is an index status.

limitations: The identity concerns the core language. The JavaScript and Web APIs, WASI, test scripting and runtimes have separate scopes. Active describes the index record.
